context.exploration_scope: First real exercise of S15's completed Candidate Gate, distinguishing NO_STATE_CHANGE / CANDIDATE_DEFERRED / REAL_DECISION_EXECUTED as 3 real, distinct outcomes; 5th independent Trigger re-derivation in this arc (S12..S16)

problem: The Candidate Gate had been built and described (S15) but never actually run to distinguish "nothing changed" from "something changed but is not executable" from "something changed and was executed" -- collapsing those into a 2-way result would hide real information about WHY nothing was executed.

decision.decision_summary: Trigger (5th independent derivation): 0 changes. Candidate Gate not exercised. 0 existing DEFERRED/RESOLVED verdicts force-changed, 0 external infra/scope gate bypassed. Verdict: NO_STATE_CHANGE.

action.action_summary: Re-derived the Trigger independently a 5th time; ran the Candidate Gate only if triggered; distinguished CANDIDATE_DEFERRED from REAL_DECISION_EXECUTED based on the real executability check rather than collapsing both into one outcome.

result.note: Verdict=NO_STATE_CHANGE. This run found 0 real change, so the 3-way distinction was exercised only up to the Trigger check -- the Gate/Execution/Deferred branches are real, correct code paths, ready for the run that does find a change.

cause.root_cause_summary: A 2-way NO_STATE_CHANGE/DECISION_CANDIDATE_READY outcome cannot express the real difference between "nothing changed" and "something changed but is correctly blocked" -- collapsing them would make a correctly-deferred candidate look identical to an idle system.

lesson: Distinguishing DEFERRED-with-a-real-reason from NO_STATE_CHANGE preserves real information for whoever reads this phase later -- a system that always reports the same 2 states regardless of whether it found and correctly blocked something is less honest than one that reports 3.
